instructions: Put the chicken in a medium pot with the red onion, sliced, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt. Cover with about 4 cups of water and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam.
Turn the heat down to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through. Lift out the chicken and let it cool. Strain the broth and keep 3/4 cup.
Remove the skin and bones and shred the meat into thin strips. Finely chop the ham and bacon.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Melt 3 tablespoons of the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk and the 3/4 cup broth a little at a time. Keep whisking over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the sauce is thick and bubbling. Take it off the heat.
Beat the egg in a small bowl and whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce. Stir it back into the saucepan with the cheese, the nutmeg, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and the pepper.
Fold in the chicken, ham and bacon. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Melt the remaining 5 tablespoons butter. Brush an 8 inch square baking dish with butter and lay in 4 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter and letting the edges hang over the sides.
Spread the filling over the phyllo and fold the overhanging edges in over it.
Lay the remaining 3 sheets on top, scrunching each loosely. Brush with the rest of the butter, sprinkle with the sesame seeds, and poke a few holes in the top for steam.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until the top is deep golden and crisp. Let it rest for 10 minutes, then cut into squares.
To keep it, cool the leftovers, cover, and refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat squares in a 350°F oven for 15 to 20 minutes, until hot in the middle and crisp on top..
method_notes: Lead is My Greek Dish (4.91 from 606): chicken poached with onions, a cheesy bechamel, ham and bacon, baked between buttered phyllo sheets. Its amounts are for a big tray of 8 to 10 pieces, so everything here is halved for an 8 inch pan. The recipe lists no stock but its method adds 1 1/2 cups, so the poaching broth is used. Dimitra's Dishes uses roasted thighs, roasted red peppers and three cheeses with no ham, and bakes a bigger tray. It is a pie that reheats well, so the keeping and reheating line is the last step.
